captionCopy:
**Ridd:** Is this the **first project** that you've taken on as a freelancer where you're—

**James:** Yeah. Yeah, yeah.

**Ridd:** Dude, how cool is that?

**James:** For the longest time, honestly, I was always so **jealous** of engineers being able to build ideas. Or not even jealous, sometimes **frustrated**, because maybe an engineer doesn't quite do what you envision, the idea you have in your mind.

So being able to actually put an idea together from **zero to one** and build it, like I said, really **empowers** me to do a lot more of that. It's such an exciting time for designers in the same boat as me. I've never been a **technical designer** whatsoever. I think I've mentioned that to you before. Thinking in systems, I'm just not that designer at all. But these tools **unlock** a part of the process, if you're patient enough to keep playing around and keep bringing **simple ideas** over.

I started pretty simple, just trying to build little tools that might help with animating an illustration or whatever. Starting there, the nature of the beast with these tools is things **move fast**, and you will move fast.

It's inevitable. You'll move fast, pick things up, and learn how this stuff works. So, **I'm loving it**, you know. It's so, so enjoyable working on this stuff.
